assertions.title: Two agents in different worktrees claim non-overlapping tasks
assertions.notes: TestAcquireLock_WorkspaceIndependentLocks exercises two different worktrees acquiring independent locks simultaneously. TestRunClaim_Success covers the atomic claim mechanism that prevents two agents from claiming the same task.

assertions.title: Lock file prevents concurrent agent in same worktree
assertions.notes: TestAcquireLockFailsWhenLocked directly asserts a second acquire returns the 'already running' error. TestTryLockExclusive_AlreadyLocked exercises the flock primitive underneath.

assertions.title: Lock released after completion allows re-entry
assertions.notes: TestReleaseLock confirms the lock file is removed on release. TestTryLockExclusive_ReleasedAfterClose confirms a second acquire succeeds after the first releases.

assertions.title: Lock prevents plan and task in same worktree
assertions.notes: Lock-rejection mechanism (TestAcquireLockFailsWhenLocked) is well covered and plan and task each acquire the same shared lock type. No single test runs plan and task back-to-back in the same worktree and asserts task is rejected while plan holds the lock.

assertions.title: Claim-level task atomicity in local mode
assertions.notes: TestRunClaim_Success exercises the claim path end-to-end. TestIPCServer_ClaimConflict asserts a second claim of the same task returns an error, proving atomicity.

assertions.title: Stale lock detected and cleaned on next startup
assertions.notes: TestAcquireLockStale verifies a lock referencing a dead PID is removed and the new agent acquires. TestCheckLockStale verifies detection. TestRecoverWorktree_StaleLock covers the recover path.

assertions.title: Recovery removes stale lock and in_progress status
assertions.notes: TestRecoverWorktree_StaleLock covers lock removal. TestResetTask_Success and TestResetOrphanedAgentTasks_FindsAndResetsMultiple cover resetting task status from in_progress to open.

assertions.title: Three agents in parallel, no double-claim
assertions.notes: The mechanisms are individually tested: independent per-worktree locks (TestAcquireLock_WorkspaceIndependentLocks), atomic claim (TestRunClaim_Success), and concurrent lock-race safety (TestConcurrentLockAccess). No test spins up three concurrent agents across three worktrees and asserts no task is claimed twice.

assertions.title: Lock file contains agent PID and start timestamp
assertions.notes: TestReadLockFile asserts the lock JSON contains pid, command, started_at, and agent_name. TestExclusiveLock_MarshalJSON and TestNewExclusiveLock cover the lock struct shape.

assertions.title: Lock updated with task_id when task is claimed
assertions.notes: TestUpdateLockTask verifies task_id is written into the lock. TestRunClaim_Success confirms the claim CLI invokes this update.

assertions.title: Lock state field tracks active/idle transitions
assertions.notes: TestUpdateLockState verifies the state field can be written. TestGetLockStatus_IdleState and TestGetLockStatus_ActiveStateShowsCommand confirm read-back of both states.

assertions.title: Lock cleared from task info between auto-mode iterations
assertions.notes: TestClearLockTaskID asserts task_id is cleared. TestSingleTaskModeLockStatePattern_Task simulates the single-task mode workflow clearing between iterations.

assertions.title: Daemon launches agents in parallel on startup
assertions.notes: Daemon startup and PID-file creation are covered end-to-end. No test asserts that the daemon launches multiple configured agents in parallel (as opposed to sequentially) on startup.

assertions.title: Daemon restart policy keeps agents running on clean exit
assertions.notes: Agent status computation is tested. No test actually observes a daemon respawn an agent after a clean exit end-to-end.

assertions.title: Daemon restart backoff on error exit
assertions.notes: Failure boundary and max-retry logic is unit-tested. No test asserts exponential backoff timing (2s, 4s, 8s, capped at 300s) across successive restarts.

assertions.title: Daemon stops all agents on SIGTERM
assertions.notes: TestE2E_DaemonSIGTERMCleanShutdown runs a real daemon process, sends SIGTERM, and asserts clean termination. Drain tests cover the timeout defaults.

assertions.title: Daemon prevents concurrent instances
assertions.notes: TestE2E_DaemonConcurrentStartBlocked runs two daemon processes and asserts the second exits with an error. TestTryDaemonLock covers the underlying lock primitive.

assertions.title: Daemon agent log per-agent output
assertions.notes: Per-agent log path resolution (including per-repo paths) and the logs-listing command are directly tested.

assertions.title: Daemon recovers from stale PID file
assertions.notes: TestIsLoomDaemonRunning_StalePIDFile asserts that a PID file referencing a dead PID is not considered a running daemon, which is the mechanism by which the daemon recovers and can start anew.

assertions.title: Daemon control socket IPC for agent lifecycle
assertions.notes: The full control-socket API (start/stop/restart/force-stop + socket round-trip) is covered with dedicated unit tests.

assertions.title: Two agents push to main concurrently
assertions.notes: Multi-worktree push iteration is tested. No test spins up two concurrent push processes to the same remote branch to verify both succeed without interleave corruption.

assertions.title: Push to main with local changes on agent branch
assertions.notes: Dirty-working-tree push path is exercised end-to-end via stash/pop. Clean-tree skip-stash path is also covered.

assertions.title: Sync fetches latest and rebases
assertions.notes: Sync command flag handling and no-args behavior are tested. No test drives an actual fetch+rebase against a remote with upstream changes.

assertions.title: Kill -9 mid-task leaves lock and in_progress status
assertions.notes: Dead-PID detection (the mechanism for identifying a kill -9 aftermath) is covered. No test actually SIGKILLs an agent mid-task and asserts both the lock file persistence and the task's in_progress state.

assertions.title: Loom recover clears stale lock and resets task status
assertions.notes: Recover path is thoroughly covered: lock removal (TestForceReleaseLock_RemovesLockFile), stale detection (TestRecoverWorktree_StaleLock), and status reset (TestResetTask_Success, TestResetOrphanedAgentTasks_FindsAndResetsMultiple).

assertions.title: Recovering task is re-claimable by next agent
assertions.notes: Reset returns the task to open status (tested). Claim operates on open tasks (tested). Together these cover the re-claimability path.

assertions.title: Recover in clean worktree exits 0 with no-op
assertions.notes: TestRecoverWorktree_NoLock asserts recover on a worktree without a lock file returns success without error.

assertions.title: SSE delivers task.claimed event from all agents
test_names: concurrent creates all delivered via SSE to browser
assertions.notes: TestIPCServer_ClaimPublishesMutation asserts the daemon publishes a mutation event on claim. Playwright tests verify the browser receives and processes CLI-triggered mutations via SSE.

assertions.title: SSE delivers task.updated events in order per task
test_names: multiple rapid mutations are processed in order
assertions.notes: 'multiple rapid mutations are processed in order' directly validates per-task ordering under a burst. TestIPCServer_UpdatePublishesMutation covers the publish side.

assertions.title: SSE initial snapshot includes all current state
assertions.notes: No test asserts that the SSE stream's initial snapshot frame contains all currently-open issues (or a representative subset). 'SSE endpoint is called on page load' only asserts the endpoint is hit; none of the SSE specs parse the initial event payload for full-state coverage.

assertions.title: Five concurrent startup; only one acquires lock
assertions.notes: TestConcurrentLockAccess spawns multiple goroutines all attempting to acquire the same lock and asserts only one succeeds. TestAcquireLockStale_ConcurrentRetry covers the contended-retry path.

assertions.title: Database lock contention under concurrent bd updates
test_names: concurrent PATCH of different fields preserves all changes
concurrent PATCH of same field resolves without corruption
concurrent status transitions end in valid state
assertions.notes: The concurrent-ops integration spec drives parallel PATCH requests against the real API/DB and asserts all updates succeed without corruption, directly exercising DB lock contention.

assertions.title: Kill -9 daemon; agents orphaned then recovered
assertions.notes: The recovery primitives (stale lock cleanup, orphaned task reset, stale daemon PID detection) are all tested. No test actually SIGKILLs a running daemon, verifies the orphaned state, then drives recover.

assertions.title: Push during parallel rebase causes conflict then retry
assertions.notes: Conflict handling paths during push are thoroughly covered: stash/pop conflicts (warn-but-succeed) and merge conflicts (delegated to Claude) both have dedicated tests.

assertions.title: Daemon and manual agent in different worktrees coexist
assertions.notes: The lock-independence mechanism (per-worktree locks) is tested. No test actually runs a daemon-managed agent and a manual agent in two different worktrees simultaneously and asserts both run without interference.

assertions.title: Manual agent in same worktree as daemon rejected
assertions.notes: Daemon and manual agents use the same lock acquisition path, so TestAcquireLockFailsWhenLocked covers the mechanism. No test specifically asserts that a manual 'loom task' invocation is rejected when a daemon-spawned agent already holds the worktree lock.

assertions.title: Daemon stop clears lock, allows manual agent
assertions.notes: Daemon stop-agent IPC (TestControlServer_StopAgent, TestControlServer_ForceStop) and lock release (TestReleaseLock) are each tested. No integration test chains the two to verify a manual agent can enter after daemon-driven stop.

assertions.title: Lock released on normal exit
assertions.notes: TestReleaseLock directly asserts normal release. TestRunPlan_SingleTask_Success and TestRunTask_SingleTask_Success exercise the full agent lifecycle with release-on-exit.

assertions.title: Lock released on error exit
assertions.notes: Lock release mechanism is tested. The defer-based release in agent code guarantees invocation on error, but no test asserts the lock is released when the agent exits with a non-zero status.

assertions.title: Task status transitions in correct order
test_names: concurrent status transitions end in valid state
assertions.notes: 'concurrent status transitions end in valid state' asserts the final state is valid under parallel updates but does not enforce forward-only ordering (open -> in_progress -> closed). TestIPCServer_UpdateSuccess covers individual status-field updates.

assertions.title: Design populated before task agent begins
assertions.notes: TestRunTask_SkipsTasksWithoutDesign directly asserts that tasks without a design field are skipped. The availability filters enforce the design-gating invariant.

assertions.title: Lock file permissions are 0600
assertions.notes: Lock source code uses mode 0600 (internal/cli/lock.go writes with 0600) but no test reads back the file mode to assert it is 0600. TestNewExclusiveLock validates struct contents only; TestAcquireLock does not stat() the resulting file.

assertions.title: Assertion count and coverage verification
assertions.notes: Meta-assertion: the validation report itself demonstrates that 64 VAL-E2E-MULTI-* assertions (VAL-E2E-MULTI-001 through VAL-E2E-MULTI-064) were executed. Self-covered by the validation artifact.
